questions.stem: A 3-month-old has poor feeding, diaphoresis, tachypnea, and persistent tachycardia after a febrile illness. Lung exam shows crackles. Which additional chest radiograph finding would strengthen suspicion for cardiac failure rather than isolated lower respiratory infection?

options.D: Normal cardiac silhouette with peribronchial cuffing

questions.rationale: Cardiomegaly in the setting of congestion and heart-failure signs supports cardiac dysfunction.

option_explanations.A: Correct. It supports cardiac enlargement and heart failure.
option_explanations.B: More typical of obstructive airway disease.
option_explanations.D: Can occur with viral respiratory illness and does not support cardiac enlargement.

questions.board_pearl: Cardiomegaly is not required for myocarditis, but when present with congestion it is a useful clue.

questions.stem: A 12-year-old has months of exercise intolerance and cardiomegaly, but no recent illness. Echo shows a markedly dilated LV with chronic remodeling. Troponin is normal. Which diagnosis becomes more likely than acute myocarditis?
questions.rationale: A chronic time course with marked chamber dilation/remodeling and no evidence of acute myocardial injury favors dilated cardiomyopathy over acute myocarditis.

option_explanations.A: Correct. Chronic remodeling and prolonged symptoms fit DCM.
option_explanations.B: Pericarditis is typically an acute inflammatory syndrome.
option_explanations.C: Age and chronic cardiac findings do not fit.
option_explanations.D: Would present acutely and does not cause chronic LV dilation.
option_explanations.E: Kawasaki disease is an acute vasculitis syndrome, usually in younger children.

questions.board_pearl: Time course and degree of remodeling help distinguish acute inflammatory dysfunction from chronic cardiomyopathy.

questions.stem: A 7-year-old with myocarditis has frequent ventricular premature beats but remains normotensive. What is the best next step?

options.A: Stop telemetry because ectopy is expected
options.B: Continue close rhythm monitoring and reassess ventricular function/hemodynamics
options.C: Discharge if the child is asymptomatic
options.E: Ignore the rhythm if troponin is decreasing

questions.rationale: Ventricular ectopy reflects electrical involvement and may precede more serious arrhythmias, so continued monitoring is appropriate.

option_explanations.A: Electrical instability should not be dismissed.
option_explanations.B: Correct. Rhythm and hemodynamic surveillance are warranted.
option_explanations.C: Current arrhythmia risk argues against discharge.
option_explanations.D: Exercise should be restricted during active myocarditis.
option_explanations.E: Biomarker trends do not eliminate arrhythmic risk.

questions.board_pearl: In myocarditis, a reassuring blood pressure does not make ventricular ectopy benign.

questions.stem: A 5-year-old with myocarditis is receiving treatment in the PICU. Which new finding most clearly indicates worsening end-organ perfusion?

options.B: Decreasing urine output with rising lactate

questions.rationale: Oliguria and rising lactate indicate inadequate systemic perfusion and worsening shock.

option_explanations.A: Tachycardia is important but less specific for end-organ failure.
option_explanations.B: Correct. These are direct markers of impaired perfusion.
option_explanations.C: Fever is not an end-organ perfusion marker.
option_explanations.D: Congestion may persist without proving worsening output.

questions.board_pearl: Track perfusion, not just heart rate, when assessing trajectory in cardiogenic shock.

questions.stem: A 15-year-old recovering from myocarditis reports new exertional palpitations during a gradual return to activity. What is the best next step?

options.A: Continue increasing exercise because palpitations are common
options.B: Stop exertion and obtain prompt cardiac reassessment
options.D: Ignore symptoms if resting ECG was previously normal

questions.rationale: New exertional palpitations after myocarditis may signal residual arrhythmia and should prompt cessation of activity and reassessment.

option_explanations.A: Could expose the patient to arrhythmic risk.
option_explanations.B: Correct. Symptoms during return-to-play require reevaluation.
option_explanations.C: Caffeine may worsen palpitations and does not address the cause.
option_explanations.D: A prior normal ECG does not exclude intermittent arrhythmia.
option_explanations.E: Competition is not safer than practice.

questions.board_pearl: New chest pain, palpitations, syncope, or disproportionate dyspnea during recovery warrants renewed evaluation.

questions.stem: A 9-year-old with suspected myocarditis is too unstable to undergo sedated cardiac MRI safely. Which approach is most appropriate?

options.A: Delay stabilization until MRI is obtained
options.B: Use clinical findings, ECG, biomarkers, and echocardiography while prioritizing stabilization
options.C: Exclude myocarditis because MRI cannot be performed
options.E: Discharge and schedule MRI next month

questions.rationale: CMR is valuable but should not supersede stabilization. Myocarditis can be clinically suspected using other modalities when MRI is unsafe or unavailable.

option_explanations.B: Correct. Diagnosis is multimodal and management should not wait for CMR.
option_explanations.C: MRI is not mandatory for every clinical diagnosis.
option_explanations.D: Exercise testing is inappropriate in unstable disease.
option_explanations.E: The patient is unstable and cannot be discharged.

questions.board_pearl: Advanced imaging should never delay treatment of an unstable child.

questions.stem: A 13-year-old develops myocarditis while taking a newly started medication known to cause hypersensitivity reactions. He also has rash and eosinophilia. Which etiologic category deserves particular consideration?
questions.rationale: A temporal medication relationship plus systemic hypersensitivity findings should raise concern for drug-associated inflammatory myocardial injury.

option_explanations.A: Correct. The systemic allergic phenotype is the clue.
option_explanations.B: Does not explain rash, eosinophilia, and acute myocardial injury.
option_explanations.C: Athletic remodeling does not cause inflammatory findings.
option_explanations.E: Would not cause this hypersensitivity syndrome.

questions.board_pearl: Myocarditis has noninfectious causes; medication exposure matters when the phenotype fits.

questions.stem: A 10-year-old with fulminant myocarditis has refractory cardiogenic shock despite maximal conventional medical support. Which therapy may serve as a bridge to myocardial recovery or transplantation?

options.A: VA-ECMO or another appropriate mechanical circulatory support strategy
options.E: No further escalation because myocarditis is always self-limited

questions.rationale: Mechanical circulatory support can maintain perfusion in refractory fulminant myocarditis while awaiting recovery or transplantation.

option_explanations.A: Correct. This is a key rescue strategy in severe fulminant disease.
option_explanations.E: Fulminant myocarditis can be fatal without advanced support.

questions.board_pearl: Fulminant myocarditis can recover dramatically if the circulation is supported through the acute phase.

questions.stem: Which echocardiographic finding can occur in pediatric myocarditis and should be interpreted in the clinical context?
questions.rationale: Myocarditis can produce regional or global ventricular dysfunction and can mimic ischemic patterns.

option_explanations.A: Correct. Regional abnormalities are recognized in myocarditis.
option_explanations.B: Common incidental finding and does not explain myocarditis.
option_explanations.C: Structural obstruction is a different diagnosis.

questions.board_pearl: Myocarditis does not always cause uniform global dysfunction.

questions.stem: A 17-year-old athlete with confirmed myocarditis asks why intense exercise is restricted during recovery. Which explanation is best?

options.A: Active myocardial inflammation can increase the risk of malignant arrhythmias during exertion
options.B: Exercise permanently enlarges the coronary arteries
options.E: Restriction is only intended to prevent muscle soreness

questions.rationale: Myocarditis can create electrical instability and sudden-death risk, especially during active inflammation and exertion.

option_explanations.A: Correct. Arrhythmia prevention is a major rationale for restriction.
option_explanations.D: Laboratory interpretation is not the primary reason.
option_explanations.E: The concern is cardiac safety, not musculoskeletal discomfort.

questions.board_pearl: The exercise restriction is primarily about arrhythmic and myocardial risk, not deconditioning.
